• Sender Coupling: Caller knows the action to perform.
• Side-Effect Expectation: Mutates state in recipient domain.
• Response Model: Often expects ACK or Reply Message.
• Realization: Task queue jobs, Saga command messages.

• Payload Completeness: Carries entire entity representation.
• Decoupled Action: Receiver decides how to interpret state.
• Contract Governance: Requires schema registry backward compatibility.
• Realization: CDC snapshot records, data replication streams.

div.div:
• Complete Independence: Emitter is agnostic to downstream existence.
• Immutability: Historical event cannot be altered, only compensated.
• Temporal Decoupling: Consumers consume at individual latencies.
• Realization: Kafka topic logs, AWS EventBridge domain events.

div.div:
Enterprise Construction Invariants:
• Intent Disambiguation: Do not overload Event Messages with invocation commands; events report what has occurred, commands state what must happen.
• Asynchronous Correlation: Request-Reply over queues requires immutable Correlation IDs and dynamic Return Addresses to prevent client thread pool blocking.
• TTL Bounds: Every in-flight correlation must define a client-side expiration deadline to prevent unbounded memory growth from lost response packets.
